The authenticity of the order can be re-

Economic Offences Wing, New Delhi.
The petitioner further seeks permission to travel abroad in connection with his business.

2. Mr. Prashant Mehta, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits, that the petitioner needs to travel on business to Luxembourg, Pristina in Kosova and Dusseldorf in Germany; and to that end, he seeks suspension of the effect and operation of the LOC issued against him.
3.
Issue notice.
4. Mr. Anurag Ahluwalia, learned CGSC and Mr. Sanjeev Bhandari, learned ASC appear on behalf of respondent No.1 and 2 respectively on advance copy; and accept notice.

sentences.text: 5. Learned ASC points-out, that the petitioner has not set-out his detailed itinerary nor his flight details, places of residence and contact numbers at the destinations referred to in the application.
6. To answer that Mr. Mehta undertakes to furnish all necessary particulars to the Investigating Officer ('I.O.'), within 02 days, under written acknowledgement.

7. Subject to the petitioner furnishing the required particulars to the I.O.
as above
, Mr. Bhandari seeks time to file an appropriate status report verifying the details of travel.

8. Let status report be filed before the next date; with copy to the opposing counsel.
9.
Re-notify on 25th November 2024.
10. By way of the present application filed under section 528 of the BNSS, the applicant/complainant - M/s. Selfx India Pvt. Ltd. seeks
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 23/11/2024 at 00:13:31 the leave of this to intervene in the present petition and to be heard in the matter.
11. Mr. Tanmay Mehta, learned counsel appearing for the intervention applicant submits that his limited prayer by way of the present application is that they be heard in the present proceedings.

12. In view of Jagjeet Singh & Ors. vs. Ashish Mishra @ Monu & Anr., the complainant is entitled to unbridled participatory rights at every stage of a criminal proceedings; and therefore there is no cavil with the proposition that the complainant/applicant is entitled to be heard in the present matter as well.

entities.text: Jagjeet Singh & Ors. vs. Ashish Mishra @ Monu & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However there is no requirement for the complainant to be formally impleaded as party respondent for that purpose.
13. In view thereof, the present petition is disposed-of, with the observation that complainant - M/s Selfx India Pvt. Ltd. - shall be entitled to be heard in the present petition.
14. The application stands disposed-of in the above terms.
Re - notify on 25th November 2024.
